answer.text:
The operator ID field (OP_ID) was first raised by Kwame Boateng in the September 2024 master data workshop, and the removal was proposed by Priya Nair in that same session, with Nadia Haddad agreeing to implement it at the November 2025 go/no-go call. By the time the removal was agreed, the field had already been sent outside Acme in reconciliation extracts.

Chronology:

- 24 September 2024, master data workshop: Kwame Boateng reported that the extract he received contained "a column I did not expect. There is an operator identifier on some of the movement records" . Priya Nair asked which records; Kwame said "Write-offs, mostly" . Priya then proposed removal: "We do not need to send you" it, and "Then let us take it out" . Nadia Haddad said "I do not need to receive it" . Priya called it "a five minute change. I will put it on the list" and Ana Duarte noted it as an action . This was for the ambient pilot phase; the field nonetheless continued to be sent.

- 17 November 2025, fresh go/no-go call: Priya Nair raised it again as a condition, explaining the waste write-off records carry the operator, so RELEX is "also reading who threw what away, per person, per store, per day" . Nadia Haddad confirmed RELEX receives it but does not use it, and proposed: "Then we drop it at the extract... we exclude it at source" . Priya set it as a condition, citing the works council, and Nadia committed to confirm in writing . Priya noted "It has been in every feed since February" . Lena Fischer endorsed it ("Good catch, Priya") .

- 18 November 2025: Priya confirmed in writing as "a condition rather than a request", giving examples of named operators, and asked what had been done with files already delivered .

- 19 November 2025: Nadia confirmed OP_ID is dropped at the extract from the next run (Friday night), and that already-delivered files sit in the raw landing zone and processed store, with Kwame checking downstream .

- 24 November 2025: Kwame answered: OP_ID is present in the raw landing zone for every daily file since 14 February, not carried into aggregated waste tables, but present in the June and September reconciliation extracts, two of which were emailed as attachments, once to Priya and once to a distribution list of nine people including three at Meridian. He can purge the landing zone but "I cannot purge the attachments" .

So: proposed by Priya Nair (first in September 2024, re-raised as a condition in November 2025); agreed by Nadia Haddad (implementation) with Lena Fischer endorsing; and yes, by November 2025 the field had already left Acme in emailed reconciliation extracts, including to three people at Meridian, and could not be fully recalled.
